about: One row per recorded structured-reason error, plus the registry reasons no server can raise yet. Generated by `record-fixtures.mjs` from `recorded/`; the registry it is checked against is `docs/api/reasons.md` (D611).

recorded.about: The unavailable-service path on a unary RPC: the corpus is recorded from `loams dev --no-live`, so `loams.live.v1` is not running and every one of its RPCs answers `unimplemented` with reason `feature_not_in_variant` and the variant in `metadata`. (gRPC-Web, the framing a browser sends. One length-prefixed frame: flag 0 and a zero-length message.)

The unavailable-service path on a unary RPC: the corpus is recorded from `loams dev --no-live`, so `loams.live.v1` is not running and every one of its RPCs answers `unimplemented` with reason `feature_not_in_variant` and the variant in `metadata`. (gRPC-Web carrying the proto3 JSON mapping, which a browser SDK can ask for.)

The unavailable-service path on a unary RPC: the corpus is recorded from `loams dev --no-live`, so `loams.live.v1` is not running and every one of its RPCs answers `unimplemented` with reason `feature_not_in_variant` and the variant in `metadata`. (The proto3 JSON mapping, which is what `curl` sends (design §44 §4).)

The unavailable-service path on a unary RPC: the corpus is recorded from `loams dev --no-live`, so `loams.live.v1` is not running and every one of its RPCs answers `unimplemented` with reason `feature_not_in_variant` and the variant in `metadata`. (The binary encoding, which is what an SDK sends by default.)
The unavailable-service path on a server stream: the refusal arrives inside the Connect streaming envelope, not as an HTTP status. An SDK that reports it has to read the envelope.
Decide without an idempotency key.
The same decision again, with no key to identify it.
A `failed_precondition` whose condition is **time**, not state: the approval was still pending and is no longer. The seed carries one expired approval precisely so this is reachable without waiting.

Optimistic concurrency as a *reason*: the caller decided revision 9, the server is on revision 1. An SDK surfaces this as "reload it" rather than as a generic precondition failure, because the caller can act on it.
Connect, proto3 JSON.
Connect, binary protobuf.
gRPC-Web, binary protobuf: HTTP 200, the code is in the trailers.
gRPC-Web, proto3 JSON.
SendTestNotification is a declared RPC whose handler is a stub.
Reject without a reason.
Dana decides what the agent requested on her behalf.
A session from 10 minutes ago decides a STEP_UP_SESSION approval.
Create it again: `already_exists`, which `retry_safe` callers treat as done.
A collection that is not there: `not_found` (R8).
Both `filter` and `where`: `filter_conflict`, refused before anything is read.
Create the graph.
Insert notes, tags and `TAGGED` edges with GQL and parameters, keyed.
Read it back, read-only.

The builder corpus case `search_expand`: a search that walks the graph from its hits. Without the graph feature the expand stage is refused as `invalid_argument` ("expand runs on Loams Graph, which this server does not run"), not `feature_not_in_variant`: the search itself is served.
Delete the graph.
A weighted sum with one weight for two retrievers: refused. The builders refuse it before sending; this is the server's own refusal of the raw request.
A `$1` with no value: `invalid_argument`, reason `sql_param_count`.
A statement that is not a query: `invalid_argument`.
A stream that does not exist: `not_found`.

unproducible.why: R1 needs it and no server raises it: `loams dev` has no authentication at all (`WhoAmI` answers `not_implemented`), and the mock only knows fresh and stale sessions, where stale is `step_up_required`. It arrives with the token endpoint (MT, API1 Task 7).
The mock has `revoked_principals` in its seed but no revoked device is wired to an RPC, so nothing raises it. AP0 Task 5 stubs device verification; the server side is AP4.

Decision-proof verification is a stub in `loams-apps-mock`: a request carrying a proof is refused with `not_implemented` rather than judged, because a mock that accepted an unverified proof would be teaching the wrong thing.
The pairing grant belongs to the auth plan (MT), not to AP0.
The pairing grant belongs to the auth plan (MT), not to AP0.
Push targets are `unimplemented` in the mock (AP0 Ruling 9 stub list).
Recorded, but only from `loams dev` — `loams-apps-mock` serves every package it has, so there is no variant to be outside of. That is the point of the case, and it is why the primary target keeps it.

Nothing raises the generic form: both servers answer a malformed field with a *specific* reason (`reason_required`). The generic rows below `invalid_argument` in the registry are the code-to-class mapping, so an SDK maps them from the code and needs no recording.

The mock does not validate the decision enum: an unrecognised decision value is refused as a malformed field, or not at all, but never as `invalid_decision`. The registry row is for a decision that parses and is still not one of the three legal values.

The mock answers a request with no credential `401 {"code":"unauthenticated"}` with **no `ErrorInfo`**, so the reason is genuinely absent even though it is in the registry. Recorded as `mock_status_unauthenticated`. Distinct from `token_expired` on purpose: one has a credential to refresh and the other has nothing to refresh.
Only the specific preconditions are raised (`approval_expired`, `approval_already_decided`, `approval_stale_revision`), each with a reason of its own. The generic row is the code-to-class mapping.
The mock answers `404 {"code":"not_found"}` with **no** `ErrorInfo`, so the reason is genuinely absent. Recorded as `mock_status_not_found_without_reason` so the gap is visible rather than assumed.
No naming RPC is served: `CreatePairing` and `CreateNamespace` are stubs or absent, so nothing can collide yet.
Only the specific `requester_cannot_approve` is raised today.

Backpressure and quota refusals need a loaded server. This is also the code R2 retries on, so it is the one a fault injector must synthesise (`mock_injects_retryable_errors`): no server produces it on demand.
A dependency being down. Same as above: only a fault injector can produce it on demand, which is why SDK1 Task 4 asks for one.
The caller's own deadline. Only reproducible with a delay the mock does not have.
A concurrent write winning. Needs two racing writers against one resource.
A bug. A recording of one would pin a bug that ought to be fixed.
